This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter to activate.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

This counter demonstrates state management and ARIA live regions for accessible dynamic content.

content.text:
`0.html` was already solid: it has good landmarks, focus handling, dark mode without JavaScript, print styles and a CSP. I made four small fixes instead of a rewrite. I haven't tested them in a browser.

1. **Error outline disappeared while typing:** the `input:focus` style overrode the red `[aria-invalid="true"]` border, so an invalid email field lost its red outline while you were fixing it. I moved the error rule after the focus rule and made it more specific (`:is(input, textarea)[aria-invalid="true"]`), so the red border now stays.
2. **"Sending" wasn't announced:** changing the button text to "Sending…" isn't reliably read out by screen readers. The form's status area now also says "Sending your message…", and that is replaced by the existing thank-you message when it finishes.
3. **Keyboard hint:** buttons also activate with Space, so the hint now reads "<kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> to activate".
4. **Email address in the page:** `<meta name="author">` had your email address in it, where scrapers can pick it up. I changed it to "K. Smith" to match the author name in the structured data at the top of the file. Revert this if you meant to publish the email.

Things I left alone:
- The `dns-prefetch` hints only point at sites that open in new tabs, so they don't do much.
- `canonical` still points to `example.com`, which you'll need to update before deploying.
- The dark color palette is repeated in the CSS, but that's needed for dark mode to work both when set manually and from the system setting.

`0.html` was already solid: it has good landmarks, focus handling, dark mode without JavaScript, print styles and a CSP. I made four small fixes instead of a rewrite. I haven't tested them in a browser.

1. **Error outline disappeared while typing:** the `input:focus` style overrode the red `[aria-invalid="true"]` border, so an invalid email field lost its red outline while you were fixing it. I moved the error rule after the focus rule and made it more specific (`:is(input, textarea)[aria-invalid="true"]`), so the red border now stays.
2. **"Sending" wasn't announced:** changing the button text to "Sending…" isn't reliably read out by screen readers. The form's status area now also says "Sending your message…", and that is replaced by the existing thank-you message when it finishes.
3. **Keyboard hint:** buttons also activate with Space, so the hint now reads "<kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> to activate".
4. **Email address in the page:** `<meta name="author">` had your email address in it, where scrapers can pick it up. I changed it to "K. Smith" to match the author name in the structured data at the top of the file. Revert this if you meant to publish the email.

Things I left alone:
- The `dns-prefetch` hints only point at sites that open in new tabs, so they don't do much.
- `canonical` still points to `example.com`, which you'll need to update before deploying.
- The dark color palette is repeated in the CSS, but that's needed for dark mode to work both when set manually and from the system setting.
